research_mode: official UK government and ONS primary statistical publications and methodology only; every claim carries a fail-closed limitation; no parcel result, exact incident location, candidate value, local risk score or business result claimed

sources.name: Knife-statistics scope
verified_claims: The publication covers cautions and convictions for specified knife and offensive-weapon offences in England and Wales.
limitations: It does not count every incident involving a knife or every police-recorded weapon offence.

sources.name: Knife-statistics period
verified_claims: The latest annual figures cover the year ending December 2025.
limitations: The period differs from year-ending-March police crime statistics.

sources.name: CJS case total
verified_claims: There were 21,091 knife and offensive-weapon offences formally dealt with by the CJS in the latest year.
limitations: This is a justice-system disposal count, not a count of unique incidents or locations.

sources.name: Annual change
verified_claims: The total increased by 1.8% compared with the year ending December 2024.
limitations: The change can reflect court throughput and case timing as well as offending.

sources.name: Decade change
verified_claims: The latest total was 20.7% higher than a decade earlier.
limitations: Pandemic restrictions, court backlog and industrial action affect the time series.

sources.name: Blade-possession share
verified_claims: Possession of an article with a blade or point accounted for 68% of the latest total.
limitations: An offence-type share cannot be converted into parcel risk.

sources.name: Offensive-weapon share
verified_claims: Possession of an offensive weapon accounted for 26% of the latest total.
limitations: Categories are legal disposal categories, not geospatial exposure measures.

sources.name: Threatening-offence share
verified_claims: Threatening with a knife or offensive weapon accounted for about 5% of the latest total.
limitations: Low proportions can still involve small counts and should not be over-interpreted locally.

sources.name: Immediate-custody count
verified_claims: There were 6,581 offences resulting in immediate custody.
limitations: Sentencing occasions are not necessarily unique offenders.

sources.name: Immediate-custody proportion
verified_claims: Immediate custody accounted for 31.2% of latest knife and offensive-weapon offences.
limitations: The proportion is not a probability for an individual case.

sources.name: Custody-rate annual change
verified_claims: The immediate-custody proportion was 2.6 percentage points lower than the previous year.
limitations: Case mix and offender history affect sentencing outcomes.

sources.name: Three-month-or-less share
verified_claims: Eleven percent of immediate-custody outcomes were three months or less.
limitations: Sentence bands do not identify offence severity without case context.

sources.name: Three-to-six-month share
verified_claims: Forty-five percent of immediate-custody outcomes were over three and up to six months.
limitations: Band shares should not be summed with non-custodial outcomes.

sources.name: Over-six-month share
verified_claims: Forty-four percent of immediate-custody outcomes were over six months.
limitations: The band includes a range of sentence lengths and offence circumstances.

sources.name: Average custodial sentence
verified_claims: The average immediate custodial sentence length was eight months.
limitations: An average does not describe the sentence for a specific offender.

sources.name: Threatening-offence sentence trend
verified_claims: The average custodial sentence for threatening offences was higher than a decade earlier.
limitations: Changes in law and case mix limit simple trend interpretation.

sources.name: First-time-offender share
verified_claims: Sixty-eight percent of caution and sentencing occasions involved a first knife or offensive-weapon offence.
limitations: First-time status relates to recorded cautions and convictions, not all prior behaviour.

sources.name: First-time occasion count
verified_claims: The latest year included 12,916 occasions involving first-time offenders.
limitations: Occasion counts are not exact unique-person counts for geospatial modelling.

sources.name: Child and adult separation
verified_claims: The publication separately reports adults and offenders aged 10 to 17.
limitations: Age-group outcomes must not be converted into predictions about individual children.

sources.name: Latest-release requirement
verified_claims: The publication advises users to use the latest release because figures and geography breakdowns can improve.
limitations: Historic extracts should not be mixed with revised latest-year figures.
